thread:
maria: Quick share — ran a KV spillback + eviction sweep comparing H100 (us-west) vs A100 (eu-west) with our new seqlen mix (short=8, mid=64, long=1024). TL;DR: H100 wins p50 on hit paths but shows much steeper p99 increase when misses/paging spike. Full artifacts: https://internal.redwood/bench/1719001234-kv-spillback-sweep :chart_with_upwards_trend:

ajay: Nice. can you paste the key numbers? especially p95/p99 and hit rate across the mix? :eyes:

maria: Sure — pulled the CSV head, kept the bench flags below. numbers are aggregated across 10 runs with stable load (closed-loop).

```
# run command
./run_kv_bench \  --model vicuna-33b-q4 \  --gpu h100 \  --region us-west \  --slen-mix 0.6:8,0.3:64,0.1:1024 \  --pagesize 16 \  --evict-policy lru \  --persistent_kv true
```

h100 us-west: hit_rate=0.78 | p50=42ms | p95=210ms | p99=610ms | throughput=420 req/s
a100 eu-west: hit_rate=0.74 | p50=52ms | p95=265ms | p99=820ms | throughput=380 req/s

Note: hit_rate counts logical KV hits after prefix caching. misses trigger page-in; page-in adds ~320ms median on h100, ~360ms on a100 in these runs.

devon (infra): Which kernel/autotune paths were you on? last time the h100 used kernel K1 (sliced attention) and a100 fell back to K2 (blocking).

maria: H100 used kernel K1 with async prefetch enabled. A100 landed on K2; we also tried K3 (new vectorized pager) which lowered p95 by ~12% on long seqs but slightly increased short p50 due to overhead. Kernel config snippet: 

```
kernel_override: {
  h100: K1
  a100: K2
  try_K3: true
}
paging: { async_prefetch: true, max_inflight_pages: 8 }
```

noah (sre): Did you test persistent_kv=false? curious about cold-start paging pressure when hosts restart.

maria: Yes — persistent_kv=false (stateless) increases p99 by ~28% on long sequences for both GPUs. With persistent=true, we see lower variance and cold-restart p99 reduced ~200-400ms depending on region.

liyah: Any quality regressions from q4 quantization on long context? we care about hallucinations for long-context retrieval flows. :thinking_face:

maria: Ran the automated eval set + 50 manual long-context cases. No meaningful drop on short/mid. For very long (>=1024) we observed a tiny bump in hallucination rate (2% -> 3.5%) when pages are heavily evicted and rehydrated mid-generation. Filed GH-456: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/issues/456 :spiral_notepad:

ajay: Could you attach the latency heatmaps by sequence bucket? want to see how hit_rate maps to p99 contours.

maria: Uploaded SVGs in the artifacts link. quick ascii summary below (slen buckets: 8 / 64 / 1024):

H100-us-west: hit_rate by bucket = [0.85, 0.72, 0.40] | p99 by bucket = [120ms, 430ms, 1200ms]
A100-eu-west: hit_rate by bucket = [0.83, 0.68, 0.36] | p99 by bucket = [160ms, 560ms, 1400ms]

infra-bot: CI bench job #232 started for run 1719001234 (compare: K1 vs K3, persistent_kv toggle)

devon (infra): Actionable items: 1) run K3 baseline on H100 with larger prefetch window (max_inflight_pages=16) 2) repeat A/B with cross-region fan-in (clients from eu hitting us-west) 3) check NUMA config on A100 hosts (we might be under-threaded).

maria: Agreed. I'll queue the K3+prefetch sweep and a cross-region fan-in job. Putting expected ETA end of day tomorrow. will post updated CSVs and a short summary in #eng-ml when done. :thumbsup:

noah (sre): Also capture system-level metrics (PCIe stalls, page fault counts). last time those correlated with p99 spikes.

maria: Will include dmesg+nvml dumps in artifacts. thanks!

ajay: Great thread. Once we have K3 numbers we can update the routing policy recommendation for region/tier.

maria: Yep — goal: explicit policy: prefer h100/K1 for latency-sensitive hit-heavy workloads, fallback to a100/K3 for throughput-y long-seq backfills. I'll draft a short doc after the follow-ups.
